sop_modules.name: Setup -- Tread Protection, Floor Protection, Wall Masking, Spray Containment, Carpet Runner Protection, Safety Signage
sop_modules.description: Combined setup module consolidating protection tasks from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC (MOD_STRS_SETUP) and SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC (MOD_STRL_SETUP). Tread protection is FIRST task and mandatory at all tiers. In RP occupied context, tread walkability is critical -- residents use stairs daily. Floor protection at landings (almost always finished floors in RP). Wall masking for spray method. Spray containment (cardboard shields behind balusters, Tape & Drape). Carpet runner protection if present (RP-specific). Safety signage for occupied homes (RP-specific).

tasks.name: Install Tread Protection (Ram Board Stair Armor)
tasks.description: FIRST task -- before any other work. Install Ram Board Stair Armor or equivalent non-slip protection on all treads. Secure with low-tack Safe-Release tape. NEVER use plastic sheeting -- extreme fall hazard per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2. In RP occupied context, protection must remain walkable throughout multi-day project. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_TREAD_PROTECT + TSK_STRL_TREAD_PROTECT_VERIFY.

quality_notes.all: Every tread covered. Non-slip surface verified. Secured with low-tack tape. No gaps between treads.

tasks.name: Install Landing Floor Protection
tasks.description: Canvas drop cloth runners at landing areas (top and bottom of stairway). In RP, landing floors are almost always finished. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_FLOOR_PROTECT + TSK_STRL_FLOOR_PROTECT.

quality_notes.all: Drop cloth covers landing work area. Edges secured.

tasks.name: Mask Walls Along Stringer Edge and Railing Area
tasks.description: Tape & mask walls adjacent to stringer and railing system. Required for spray method (full masking). In RP, may also be needed for brush method near stringer-to-wall junction since walls are always finished (SS_PAINTED_*). Consolidated from TSK_STRS_WALL_MASK + TSK_STRL_WALL_MASK.

quality_notes.all: Wall masking along full stringer length and railing area. Clean tape edge at stringer-to-wall junction.

tasks.name: Set Up Baluster Spray Containment
tasks.description: Cardboard shields behind balusters, small torn tape pieces at baluster-rail junctions. Tape & Drape pre-taped plastic along walls. HVLP preferred over airless for in-place baluster work -- significantly less overspray per doctrine 6.3. 45+ min setup for typical 39-62 baluster system. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_CONTAIN.

quality_notes.all: All balusters shielded. Junction tape in place. Wall masking complete. Containment verified before spray.

tasks.name: Protect Carpet Runner
tasks.description: RP-specific: occupied homes may have carpet runner on stairs. Rosin paper over carpet edges where paint work occurs. Secure with low-tack Safe-Release tape to avoid carpet backing damage. Not present in NC (carpet installed after painting). RP_NEW task.

quality_notes.all: Carpet edges protected at all paint work zones. Low-tack tape on carpet backing.

tasks.name: Install Wet Paint Safety Signage
tasks.description: RP-specific for occupied homes. Install wet paint warning signs at top and bottom of stairway. Critical for resident safety -- stairs are the primary circulation path. Signs must remain visible throughout project. RP_NEW task.

quality_notes.all: Signs visible at both stairway access points. Clear 'WET PAINT' messaging.

tasks.name: Remove Handrail Brackets (Label and Bag)
tasks.description: QT4+ only. Remove handrail brackets, label each piece, bag hardware. Mark locations. Allows handrail to be finished horizontally (reduces runs/sags) and paint behind attachment points. At QT3 brackets are masked in place. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRACKET_REMOVE. Per doctrine 12.1.

quality_notes.all: All brackets removed, labeled, bagged. Locations marked. No wall damage.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Tread protection (FIRST -- mandatory) -> Floor protection (landings) -> Carpet runner protection (if present) -> Wall masking (spray or brush near finished walls) -> Spray containment (spray only) -> Bracket removal (QT4+) -> Safety signage. All setup complete before assessment begins.

sop_modules.name: Condition Assessment -- Inspect All Components, Adhesion Test, Coating ID, Anti-Slip Verification
sop_modules.description: RP-specific assessment phase. 100% RP_NEW tasks -- no NC equivalent. Visual condition scan of all 6 stair component types (risers, stringers, balusters, newels, handrails, base rails). ASTM D3359 adhesion test at representative sections. Coating identification (latex vs alkyd -- stair components historically received oil-based enamel for durability). Anti-slip verification of tread protection adequacy. Assessment results drive downstream task activation: primer selection, prep intensity, contamination treatment. All tasks are FIXED time per stairway system.

tasks.name: Visual Condition Inspection -- All Stair Components
tasks.description: Scan all stair components with work light: risers, stringers, balusters, newels, handrails, base rails. Map cracking, peeling, adhesion failure, wear patterns, staining, moisture damage per component type. Assign condition_scale (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) per component. Different components may have different states -- handrails (high wear) may be FAIR while risers (low touch) are GOOD. Photograph defects. Document scope of scraping, feathering, and treatment needed.

quality_notes.QT3: Standard visual with work light, document visible defects across all component types
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan with raking light, photograph all defect areas, per-component condition assignment
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, multiple passes, raking light, full photographic documentation per component type

tasks.name: Adhesion Test (ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Tape Test)
tasks.description: Perform cross-hatch tape test per ASTM D3359 at representative sections of each component type. Critical for stairs due to high-wear surfaces (handrails, risers at toe-kick zone) and historically oil-painted components. Test at minimum 1 location each: riser, stringer, baluster, handrail. Results determine if adhesion primer is required.

quality_notes.all: Test at minimum 4 locations (1 per major component type). Record pass/fail per ASTM D3359 classification.

tasks.name: Coating Identification -- Latex vs Oil
tasks.description: Determine existing coating type via solvent test: denatured alcohol or mineral spirits rub test. Critical for stair components -- historically received oil-based enamel for durability, especially railings and handrails. Latex over oil without adhesion primer is a primary adhesion failure mode on stairs. Test each component type separately -- some may have been previously repainted with different products.

quality_notes.all: Test at minimum 2 locations (riser + handrail). Document result: latex or alkyd per component type.

tasks.name: Anti-Slip Verification -- Tread Protection Adequacy
tasks.description: Verify tread protection material is non-slip and properly secured. Check that tread surface is not compromised. RP-specific safety assessment for occupied homes where residents use stairs daily. Verify no exposed slippery surfaces (no plastic sheeting per doctrine). Assess tread condition for any defects that could cause trip hazard during or after painting.

quality_notes.all: All treads verified safe and walkable. No exposed slippery surfaces. Protection integrity confirmed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Condition scan (all component types) -> Adhesion test (representative sections) -> Coating ID (latex vs oil) -> Anti-slip verification. Assessment results determine which prep and prime tasks activate downstream.

sop_modules.name: Lead-Safe RRP Containment (Shared Module)
sop_modules.description: Shared lead-safe work practice module for all interior RP specs. Conditional on home built before 1978. Stair components are HIGH RISK for lead paint -- historically oil-based, typically multi-layer from multiple repaints. Includes lead test, containment setup, HEPA vacuum, containment removal, and waste disposal. This module is NOT owned by this spec -- it is a shared module referenced by all interior RP specs.

tasks.name: Lead Test (XRF or Swab)
tasks.description: Perform lead test at representative areas. XRF preferred; lead swab test acceptable. Test at minimum 1 riser + 1 stringer + 1 handrail + 1 baluster. Stair components are high-risk for lead paint -- often last surfaces to transition from oil to latex, frequently multi-layer from multiple repaints.

tasks.name: RRP Containment Setup
tasks.description: Install containment: poly sheeting on floors and openings at stairwell access points, warning signs at entry points, restrict entry to certified personnel only. Stairwell containment is more complex than room containment due to open vertical shaft. Per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745.

tasks.name: HEPA Vacuum After Paint Disturbance
tasks.description: HEPA vacuum all surfaces after each sanding/scraping disturbance to capture lead-contaminated dust. Required by EPA RRP Rule. On stairs, dust settles on treads below work area -- HEPA vacuum treads and landings after each disturbance cycle.

tasks.name: RRP Containment Removal and Visual Clearance
tasks.description: Remove containment poly sheeting from stairwell access points, perform visual clearance inspection. No visible dust or debris on treads, landings, or adjacent surfaces. Dispose containment materials per EPA RRP waste handling rules.

tasks.name: Lead-Contaminated Waste Disposal
tasks.description: Package and dispose of lead-contaminated debris, containment materials, and cleaning supplies per EPA RRP Rule. Label and transport to approved disposal facility.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Lead test first -> If positive: containment setup -> All prep tasks use wet methods -> HEPA vacuum after each disturbance -> Containment removal after all prep complete -> Waste disposal.

sop_modules.name: Prep -- TSP Wash, Degloss (Per Component), Scrape/Feather, Mildew Treatment, Caulk Assess/Replace, Dust Removal
sop_modules.description: Condition-driven prep module for all stair components. GOOD condition: TSP wash + degloss + dust wipe. FAIR condition: add scrape/feather, caulk assess/replace. POOR condition: full scrape, extensive feathering, contamination treatment. Degloss replaces NC sand_prep (existing paint vs bare wood). Canonical painting sequence within module: stringers -> risers -> balusters -> newels -> handrails -> base rails. Dual UOM: EA for risers, balusters, newels; LF for stringers, handrails, base rails.

tasks.name: TSP Wash All Stair Component Surfaces
tasks.description: TSP (trisodium phosphate) wash of all stair component surfaces to remove hand oils (especially handrails), cleaning chemical residue, dust, and surface contaminants. Wipe on with rag, scrub detail areas (baluster junctions, newel caps), rinse, allow to dry. Required before degloss or coating application when contamination is present. RP_NEW task -- not in NC.

quality_notes.all: All contaminated surfaces washed. Rinse verified clean. Dry before next task.

tasks.name: Mildew/Biocide Treatment
tasks.description: Apply bleach or mildewcide solution to mildew-affected stair component areas. Rare on stairs but possible in basement stairwells or near exterior doors. Allow full contact/kill time per product directions. Rinse and allow 24 hr dry before priming. Source moisture must already be resolved.

quality_notes.all: All mildew killed. No visible mildew remains. Surface clean and dry.

tasks.name: Degloss Stringer Surfaces
tasks.description: Chemical degloss (liquid sander wipe-on) or mechanical scuff (150-180 grit) on stringer/skirtboard surfaces. Stringers first per canonical sequence (#4). Chemical degloss preferred for open stringer notch profiles -- reaches crevices that sanding blocks cannot. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRS_SAND_PREP_STRINGER -- different purpose: NC sands bare substrate, RP deglosses existing finish.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss -- chemical or mechanical, all accessible stringer surfaces
quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification on open stringer profiles
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss with verification and spot adhesion re-test

tasks.name: Degloss Riser Surfaces
tasks.description: Chemical degloss or mechanical scuff on riser faces. Risers after stringers per canonical sequence (#8). Flat vertical surfaces -- mechanical scuff with sanding sponge is efficient. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRS_SAND_PREP_RISER.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss -- chemical or mechanical, full riser face

tasks.name: Degloss Baluster Surfaces
tasks.description: Chemical degloss or mechanical scuff on baluster surfaces. Balusters after risers per canonical sequence (#5). Rate varies dramatically by profile type: square balusters are simple flat surfaces; turned balusters have complex curves requiring chemical deglosser (faster than mechanical on profiles, no sanding dust). Baluster_profile modifier applies: square=1.0x, turned=1.75x. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_SAND_PREP_BALUSTER + TSK_STRL_SCUFF_SAND_IRON.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss -- chemical preferred for turned profiles
quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification at baluster-rail junctions
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss with verification, all profile surfaces addressed

tasks.name: Degloss Newel Post Surfaces
tasks.description: Chemical degloss or mechanical scuff on newel posts. Newels after balusters per canonical sequence (#6). Larger surface area with decorative detail (caps, rosettes, flutes). Chemical degloss preferred for detail areas. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_SAND_PREP_NEWEL.

quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss including caps, rosettes, and detail areas
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss with verification, all decorative detail addressed

tasks.name: Degloss Handrail Surfaces
tasks.description: Chemical degloss or mechanical scuff on handrails -- all 4 surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside). Handrails after newels per canonical sequence (#7). QT4+: handrails may be horizontal (brackets removed) for easier degloss. Chemical degloss preferred for profiled handrails. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_SAND_PREP_HANDRAIL.

quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification, underside addressed
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss all surfaces with verification

tasks.name: Degloss Base Rail Surfaces
tasks.description: Chemical degloss or mechanical scuff on base rails. Conditional -- not all railing systems have base rails. Same degloss protocol as handrails. After handrails in sequence. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_SAND_PREP_BASE_RAIL.

tasks.name: Scrape Loose Paint and Feather Edges -- Risers and Stringers
tasks.description: Scrape all failing, peeling, flaking, or loose paint from riser faces and stringer surfaces. Feather-sand all scrape edges to create smooth transition. Risers are relatively easy flat surfaces but contained between treads. Stringers are long diagonal runs -- open stringers require contour scraping of notch profiles. Condition-gated: only fires for FAIR/POOR conditions (SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_INT_PEELING). RP_NEW task.

quality_notes.QT3: Remove all failing paint, feather edges -- no visible ridge at 6 ft
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive scrape + near-invisible feathering at 3 ft
quality_notes.QT5: Critical scrape + perfect feathering -- no ridge at arm's length

tasks.name: Scrape Loose Paint and Feather Edges -- Balusters, Newels, Handrails
tasks.description: Scrape all failing, peeling, flaking, or loose paint from railing components. Extremely labor-intensive for turned balusters -- each baluster is a separate scrape/feather operation on complex profiles. Handrails have 4-surface access; grip area most prone to wear failure. Newels have decorative detail that traps failing paint. Baluster_profile modifier applies. Condition-gated: FAIR/POOR only. RP_NEW task.

quality_notes.QT3: Remove all failing paint from railing components, feather edges
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive scrape + near-invisible feathering, all components
quality_notes.QT5: Critical scrape + perfect feathering on all profile surfaces

tasks.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk -- Stringer-to-Wall Junction
tasks.description: Inspect existing caulk at stringer-to-wall junction along full length. Remove and replace cracked, shrunk, or failed sections. RP differs from NC -- NC applies new caulk to bare joints; RP assesses existing and replaces only failed sections (15-30% typically). Closed stringers only -- highly visible junction. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRS_CAULK_STRINGER_WALL.

quality_notes.QT3: Replace visibly failed sections -- cracked or separated joints
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect and failed joints
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, replace all joints not in perfect condition, perfect tooled bead

tasks.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk -- Riser-to-Stringer Junctions
tasks.description: Inspect existing caulk at riser-to-stringer junctions (2 joints per riser). Remove and replace cracked, shrunk, or failed sections. RP assess-and-replace pattern (15-30% typical replacement). MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRS_CAULK_RISER_STRINGER.

quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect joints
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, all joints in perfect condition

tasks.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk -- Newel Junction Joints
tasks.description: Inspect existing caulk at newel-to-tread and newel-to-handrail junctions. Remove and replace failed sections. Typically 2-3 joints per newel. RP assess-and-replace pattern. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_CAULK_NEWEL.

quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive assessment of all newel junctions
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, all joints in perfect condition

tasks.name: Remove Sanding/Scraping Dust (Tack Cloth / Vacuum)
tasks.description: Thorough dust removal after all degloss, scraping, and feathering work. Tack cloth all component surfaces. Vacuum treads and landings. In occupied RP context, HEPA vacuum recommended for dust containment. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_CLEAN_DUST + TSK_STRL_CLEAN_DUST.

quality_notes.all: All dust removed. Surfaces clean to touch. Treads and landings vacuumed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: TSP wash (if contaminated) -> Mildew treatment (if moisture damage) -> Degloss per component in canonical sequence: stringer -> riser -> baluster -> newel -> handrail -> base rail -> Scrape/feather riser/stringer (if FAIR/POOR) -> Scrape/feather railing (if FAIR/POOR) -> Caulk assess/replace (stringer-wall, riser-stringer, newel) -> Dust removal. All prep must be complete and dry before prime.

sop_modules.name: Prime -- State-Driven Primer Application (All Components)
sop_modules.description: State-driven primer module. Primer product selection determined by substrate state: SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT skips full prime (GOOD condition, adhesion passes, compatible coating -- spot prime repairs only); SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT/PEELING uses adhesion primer (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT); SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE uses mildew-resistant primer (SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT); SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE uses shellac stain-blocker (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT). Separate prime tasks per component type following canonical sequence. MODIFIED from NC substrate-driven primers.

tasks.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Stringers
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to stringer surfaces. Stringers first per canonical sequence (#4). Primer product varies by substrate state: adhesion primer (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT) for failing/peeling, mildew-resistant (SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT) for moisture damage, shellac stain-blocker (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT) for smoke damage. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRS_PRIME_STRINGER -- different primer selection logic.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Risers
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to riser surfaces. Risers after stringers per canonical sequence (#8). Vertical surface -- thin coat, no runs. Same state-driven primer selection as stringers. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRS_PRIME_RISER.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, even film, no runs on vertical surfaces.

tasks.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Balusters
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to baluster surfaces. Balusters after risers per canonical sequence (#5). Profile complexity affects rate -- baluster_profile modifier applies (square=1.0x, turned=1.75x). German round trim brush for turned profiles. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_PRIME_BALUSTER.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, thin coats on profiles to avoid buildup in crevices.

tasks.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Newel Posts
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to newel posts. Newels after balusters per canonical sequence (#6). Larger surface area with decorative detail. All newels are wood regardless of railing_type. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_PRIME_NEWEL.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, detail areas (caps, rosettes, flutes) properly coated.

tasks.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Handrails
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to handrails. Handrails after newels per canonical sequence (#7). All 4 surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside). QT4+: handrails may be horizontal (brackets removed) for easier priming. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_PRIME_HANDRAIL.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage all 4 surfaces. Watch for runs on underside.

tasks.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Base Rails
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to base rails. Conditional -- not all railing systems have base rails. Same primer system as handrails. After handrails in sequence. MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_PRIME_BASE_RAIL.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, 3 accessible surfaces.

tasks.name: Light Sand Primer for Finish Coat Adhesion
tasks.description: 220 grit light sand entire primed surface for finish coat adhesion. Tack cloth after sanding. All primed components sanded in canonical sequence. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_SAND_PRIMER + TSK_STRL_SAND_PRIMER -- consolidated into single task.

quality_notes.all: All primed surfaces lightly sanded. Uniform scratch pattern. Tack cloth after.

tasks.name: Spot Prime Scraped/Repaired Areas
tasks.description: Apply spot primer to all scraped areas, feathered edges, caulk replacements, and patched areas. Prevents flashing from differential absorption. Used for GOOD condition when only localized areas need attention, or to supplement full prime at repair areas. Brush application regardless of method -- spot work is always brushed.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot prime all repair areas, sealed against flashing
quality_notes.QT4: Spot prime all repairs with feathered edges
quality_notes.QT5: Spot prime all repairs with wide feather, may need light sand after

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Full prime per component in canonical sequence: stringer -> riser -> baluster -> newel -> handrail -> base rail (if required by substrate state) -> Sand primer -> Spot prime repairs (independent -- used for localized repairs regardless of full-prime status). Skip full prime for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT when adhesion test passes and coating is compatible.

sop_modules.name: Interstage -- Between Coats (All Components)
sop_modules.description: Fine-finish interstage protocol at ALL quality tiers. Stairs are scrutinized surfaces requiring interstage between every coat pair. Clean work area, inspect coat, sand between coats, patch defects, spot coat repairs, tack clean. Sanding discipline: QT3=spot 220, QT4=full 220, QT5=thorough 220-320. Junction nibs at baluster-handrail connection must be removed at QT4+. Run rule: AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat. Consolidated from duplicate NC riser + railing interstage modules.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat. For prime+2finish: runs after prime, after finish coat 1. For 2finish (no prime): runs after finish coat 1. For QT5 brush 3-coat: runs after prime, after finish 1, after finish 2.

tasks.name: Clean Work Area Between Coats
tasks.description: Remove dust, debris from treads and landings. Ensure clean environment for next coat. In RP occupied context, maintain walkable stairway. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_CLEAN_AREA + TSK_STRL_CLEAN_AREA.

quality_notes.all: Work area clean. Treads walkable. No dust or debris.

tasks.name: Inspect Previous Coat -- All Components
tasks.description: Visual inspection of applied coat on all stair components. Look for dust nibs, brush marks, runs, sags, missed areas, junction nibs at baluster-handrail connections. Inspection distance and rigor vary by quality tier. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_INSPECT_COAT + TSK_STRL_INSPECT_COAT.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan at 6 ft -- obvious defects on all components
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 ft -- all visible defects marked, junction nibs flagged
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length -- zero tolerance, handrail underside checked

tasks.name: Sand Between Coats -- All Components
tasks.description: Between-coat sanding on all stair component surfaces. QT3: spot sand nibs/rough spots only with 220 grit. QT4: full 220 grit all surfaces. QT5: thorough 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern. Junction nibs at baluster-handrail connection must be removed at QT4+. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces (FFD 15.4.1). Contour sanding for turned baluster profiles. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_SAND_BETWEEN + TSK_STRL_SAND_BETWEEN.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot sand nibs/rough spots only. 220 grit.
quality_notes.QT4: Full 220 grit entire surface, all components. Junction nibs removed.
quality_notes.QT5: Thorough 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern. Every imperfection addressed.

tasks.name: Patch and Repair Marked Defects (Interstage)
tasks.description: Fill, sand, and spot-prime any defects found during interstage inspection across all stair components. Scope varies by QT. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_PATCH_DEFECTS + TSK_STRL_PATCH_DEFECTS.

quality_notes.QT4: Repair all marked defects -- visible at 3 feet
quality_notes.QT5: Repair all defects regardless of size

tasks.name: Spot Coat Patched Areas
tasks.description: Touch-up patched areas to match surrounding finish before next full coat. Brush application. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_SPOT_COAT + TSK_STRL_SPOT_COAT.

quality_notes.QT5: Spot coat all repairs -- ensure uniform film build

tasks.name: Tack Cloth All Surfaces
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth before next coat application. Critical for dust-free fine finish on all stair components. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_TACK_CLEAN + TSK_STRL_TACK_CLEAN.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal -- surfaces must be clean to touch before next coat.

tasks.name: Verify Tread Protection Integrity (Daily)
tasks.description: RP-specific daily task in occupied home context. Check integrity of tread protection at start of each work day and after each interstage cycle. Repair or replace damaged, shifted, or slipping sections. Verify walkability. Critical safety task -- residents use stairs during multi-day RP projects. RP_NEW task.

quality_notes.all: All treads verified safe. Protection secure. No gaps or slippage. Walkable.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Clean area -> Tread protection verify (RP daily) -> Inspect coat -> Sand between coats -> Patch defects (if needed) -> Spot coat (if patched) -> Tack clean. Runs after each coat except the final coat.

sop_modules.name: Finish -- Brush/Spray Finish Coats (All Components)
sop_modules.description: Finish coat application for all stair components. Separate tasks per component type following canonical sequence: stringers (#4) -> risers (#8) -> balusters (#5) -> newels (#6) -> handrails (#7) -> base rails. Brush is default for stair detail work. Spray for large-scope production (HVLP preferred for in-place baluster work). 2 coats standard (QT3-QT4), 3 coats QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3. Fine-finish coating systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). For turned balusters: German round trim brush + flow additive to prevent roping. Interstage module runs between coats.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat on Stringers
tasks.description: Brush finish coat on stringer surfaces. Stringers first per canonical sequence (#4). Apply, tip once, walk away. Consistent coverage along full length. Open stringers: follow notched profile carefully. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_BRUSH_FINISH_STRINGER.

quality_notes.all: No application defects -- no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat on Risers
tasks.description: Brush finish coat on riser faces. Risers after stringers per canonical sequence (#8). Vertical surface -- thin coat essential. Check each riser for sags before moving to next. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_BRUSH_FINISH_RISER.

quality_notes.all: No application defects -- no drips, sags, or holidays. Thin coat on vertical surface.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat on Balusters
tasks.description: Brush finish coat on balusters. Balusters after risers per canonical sequence (#5). Square: angled sash brush. Turned: German round trim brush with flow additive to prevent roping. Thin coats essential -- profile traps paint. Baluster_profile modifier applies. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRUSH_FINISH_BALUSTER.

quality_notes.all: No roping on turned profiles. Thin coats, no buildup in crevices.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat on Newel Posts
tasks.description: Brush finish coat on newel posts. Newels after balusters per canonical sequence (#6). 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush. Detail work on caps, rosettes, flutes. Thin coats on vertical surfaces. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRUSH_FINISH_NEWEL.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. Detail areas properly coated. Thin coats on vertical surfaces.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat on Handrails
tasks.description: Brush finish coat on handrails. Handrails after newels per canonical sequence (#7). All 4 surfaces: top, 2 sides, underside. QT4+: paint horizontally (brackets removed). In two-tone systems: darker rail color applied last covers overlap at baluster-rail junction. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRUSH_FINISH_HANDRAIL.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. All 4 surfaces coated. No drips on underside.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat on Base Rails
tasks.description: Brush finish coat on base rails. Conditional -- when system has base rail. After handrails in sequence. 3 accessible surfaces. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRUSH_FINISH_BASE_RAIL.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. 3 accessible surfaces coated.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat on Stringers
tasks.description: Spray finish coat on stringer surfaces. Stringers first per canonical sequence. Tight fan pattern, keep moving to avoid runs. Requires wall masking. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_SPRAY_FINISH_STRINGER.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. No orange peel. No runs.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat on Risers
tasks.description: Spray finish coat on riser faces. Risers after stringers. Light passes on vertical surface. Keep gun moving. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_SPRAY_FINISH_RISER.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. Light passes on vertical. No runs.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat on Balusters
tasks.description: Spray finish coat on balusters. HVLP preferred -- 6-8 inch distance, light passes. Cardboard shields behind each baluster. Bottom-to-top passes. Containment masking must be in place. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_FINISH_BALUSTER.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. Full profile coverage. No overspray on adjacent surfaces.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat on Newel Posts
tasks.description: Spray finish coat on newel posts. Larger target -- easier spray than balusters but more material. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_FINISH_NEWEL.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. Full coverage on decorative detail.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat on Handrails
tasks.description: Spray finish coat on handrails. Light passes on all 4 surfaces. Watch for runs on underside. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_FINISH_HANDRAIL.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. All 4 surfaces coated. No runs on underside.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat on Base Rails
tasks.description: Spray finish coat on base rails. Conditional -- when system has base rail. After handrails. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_FINISH_BASE_RAIL.

quality_notes.all: No application defects.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Finish coat in canonical sequence: stringer (brush/spray) -> riser (brush/spray) -> baluster (brush/spray) -> newel (brush/spray) -> handrail (brush/spray) -> base rail (brush/spray, conditional). Coat 1 -> Interstage -> Coat 2. At QT5 brush: Coat 2 -> Interstage -> Coat 3 (reuses same tasks). Frame and component tasks can be interleaved per canonical sequence.

sop_modules.name: Cleanup -- Final Inspect, Touch-Up, Feel Test, Poly Topcoat, Bracket Reinstall, Protection Teardown, Customer Walkthrough, Tool Clean
sop_modules.description: Full cleanup module consolidating NC riser + railing cleanup modules plus RP-specific tasks. Final inspection (all components), touch-up, handrail feel test (QT5), optional poly topcoat on handrails (QT5), bracket reinstall (QT4+), protection teardown (spray containment, wall masking, carpet protection, floor protection), tread protection removal (LAST task -- may be deferred if tread work follows), customer walkthrough (RP-specific for occupied homes), tool cleanup.

tasks.name: Final Quality Inspection -- All Components
tasks.description: Final inspection of all stair components. Check riser-to-stringer junctions, stringer-to-wall caulk lines, baluster-handrail junctions, newel detail, handrail all 4 surfaces, surface finish quality. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_FINAL_INSPECT + TSK_STRL_FINAL_INSPECT.

quality_notes.QT3: Scan for obvious defects on all components
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic review of all components and junctions
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length -- zero tolerance on all surfaces

tasks.name: Touch-Up Defects Found During Final Inspection
tasks.description: Correct any remaining defects across all stair components. Feather touch-ups into surrounding finish. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_TOUCHUP + TSK_STRL_TOUCHUP.

quality_notes.QT5: Touch-up all defects -- invisible repair standard

tasks.name: Feel Test on Handrails
tasks.description: QT5 only. Run hand along entire handrail length. Must feel glass-smooth -- no nibs, no rough spots, no drip ridges. Handrails are the most-touched surface in any home. In RP, existing handrail surface may have nibs from previous paint applications, making this test even more important. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_FEEL_TEST_HANDRAIL.

quality_notes.all: Glass-smooth feel along entire handrail length. No nibs, no rough spots, no drip ridges.

tasks.name: Apply Polyurethane Topcoat on Handrails
tasks.description: Optional QT5 upgrade. Water-based polyurethane clear coat over cured enamel finish on handrails ONLY. Provides maximum hand-oil resistance. Allow full enamel cure (24-48 hours) before poly application. In RP, the poly barrier prevents hand-oil absorption into fresh finish -- even more valuable than in NC. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_POLY_TOPCOAT_HANDRAIL.

quality_notes.all: Even poly film on all handrail surfaces. No runs. Glass-smooth finish.

tasks.name: Reinstall Handrail Brackets
tasks.description: QT4+ only. Reinstall labeled brackets in original locations. Touch-up attachment point paint after reinstall. Verify handrail is secure and operational. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRACKET_REINSTALL.

quality_notes.all: All brackets reinstalled. Touch-up complete. Handrail secure and operational.

tasks.name: Remove Spray Containment
tasks.description: Remove cardboard shields from behind balusters, remove Tape & Drape from walls. Spray method only. DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_REMOVE_SPRAY_CONTAIN.

quality_notes.all: All containment materials removed. No residue on surfaces.

tasks.name: Remove Wall Masking
tasks.description: Score tape edge before removal. Pull at 45-degree angle. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_REMOVE_WALL_MASK + TSK_STRL_REMOVE_WALL_MASK.

quality_notes.all: Clean tape removal. No paint pull. No residue on wall.

tasks.name: Remove Carpet Runner Protection
tasks.description: Remove rosin paper and low-tack tape from carpet runner. Verify no paint transfer to carpet. RP-specific companion teardown task.

quality_notes.all: Carpet protection removed. No paint transfer. No tape residue on carpet.

tasks.name: Remove Floor Protection at Landings
tasks.description: Remove canvas drops from landing areas. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_REMOVE_FLOOR_PROTECT + TSK_STRL_REMOVE_FLOOR_PROTECT.

quality_notes.all: Drops removed. Landing floors clean.

tasks.name: Remove Tread Protection
tasks.description: LAST task. Remove Ram Board Stair Armor carefully. Score tape edges. May DEFER removal if tread work (SF_STAIR_TREAD spec) follows -- tread protection continuity is critical. Verify no paint transfer to treads. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_REMOVE_TREAD_PROTECT + TSK_STRL_REMOVE_TREAD_PROTECT.

quality_notes.all: All tread protection carefully removed. No paint transfer to treads. Treads clean and safe.

tasks.name: Customer Walkthrough -- Stairway System Review
tasks.description: RP-specific post-completion review with homeowner. Walk the entire stairway system together. Verify: all components painted consistently, touch-up of wear areas complete, tread protection properly removed, handrail feels smooth to touch, baluster junction finish quality, stairway is operationally safe (treads not slippery, no paint on treads). Fixed time per stairway system (~10-15 min). RP_NEW task.

quality_notes.all: Customer satisfied with finish quality. All components reviewed. Stairway safe and operational.

tasks.name: Clean Tools and Equipment
tasks.description: Clean brushes (including German round trim brushes), spray equipment (if used), dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne products. Consolidated from TSK_STRS_TOOL_CLEANUP + TSK_STRL_TOOL_CLEANUP.

quality_notes.all: All tools cleaned. Consumables disposed. Work area clean.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspection -> Touch-up -> Feel test (QT5) -> Poly topcoat handrails (QT5, after 24-48hr cure) -> Bracket reinstall (QT4+) -> Remove spray containment (spray only) -> Remove wall masking (spray only) -> Remove carpet protection (if present) -> Remove floor protection -> Remove tread protection (LAST -- may defer) -> Customer walkthrough -> Tool cleanup.

zones.notes: Mandatory from Day 1. Ram Board Stair Armor only -- NEVER plastic sheeting (fall hazard). In RP occupied context, daily verification of walkability. Removal may be deferred if tread work follows.
Canvas drop cloth runners at landing areas. In RP, landing floors are almost always finished.
Wall masking along stringer edge and railing area. Required for spray method. May also be needed for brush near finished walls.
Cardboard shields behind balusters, Tape & Drape on walls. HVLP preferred. Spray method only.
RP-specific. Rosin paper over carpet edges at paint work zones. Not present in NC.

round_configurations.notes: Most common RP round for stairs with adhesion or contamination issues. Prime coat is state-driven.

round_configurations.description: 2 finish coats only -- no prime needed
round_configurations.notes: Skip prime when adhesion test passes, existing paint is sound, and coating is compatible. Most common residential stair repaint scenario.

round_configurations.sequence: MOD_STRP_PRIME -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(1) -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(2) -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(3)
round_configurations.notes: Maximum coat sequence. State-driven prime + 3 brush finish coats per FFD 15.10.3 + FAIR/POOR condition.
QT5 brush 3-coat sequence for GOOD condition. No prime needed per FFD 15.10.3.

workflow_sequence.standard_good_condition: MOD_STRP_SETUP -> MOD_STRP_ASSESSMENT -> MOD_STRP_PREP -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(1) -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(2) -> MOD_STRP_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.standard_fair_poor_condition: MOD_STRP_SETUP -> MOD_STRP_ASSESSMENT -> [MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT] -> MOD_STRP_PREP -> MOD_STRP_PRIME -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(1) -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(2) -> MOD_STRP_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.qt5_brush_good: MOD_STRP_SETUP -> MOD_STRP_ASSESSMENT -> MOD_STRP_PREP -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(1) -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(2) -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(3) -> MOD_STRP_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.qt5_brush_fair_poor: MOD_STRP_SETUP -> MOD_STRP_ASSESSMENT -> [MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT] -> MOD_STRP_PREP -> MOD_STRP_PRIME -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(1) -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(2) -> MOD_STRP_INTERSTAGE -> MOD_STRP_FINISH(3) -> MOD_STRP_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.notes: Assessment ALWAYS runs before prep. Prime module conditional on substrate state (skip for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT). RRP containment conditional on home pre-1978. QT5 brush adds 3rd finish coat per FFD 15.10.3. Within each coat module: canonical sequence stringers -> risers -> balusters -> newels -> handrails -> base rails.

canonical_sequence_enforcement.rule: Stringers (#4) MUST be completed before risers (#8), balusters (#5) before newels (#6), newels before handrails (#7) within every module
canonical_sequence_enforcement.rationale: Painting stringers first avoids contact with wet riser surfaces when moving between treads. Painting balusters before handrails allows darker rail color (in two-tone systems) applied last to cover overlap at baluster-rail junction.

task_count_summary.notes: 64 STRP-prefixed tasks + 5 shared RRP tasks = 69 total. Slightly above the 60-task projection due to per-component degloss tasks (7 including base rail) and separate brush/spray finish variants (12). The per-component task granularity follows the NC convention pattern from both source specs. Corrected from 68 during QA (7+4+5+14+8+7+12+12 = 69).
